los.text: Describe the signs and symptoms, differential diagnoses, investigations and treatment principles of IBS, IBD and bacterial overgrowth (focus on IBD)
los.html:
Crohn's diseaseUlcerative colitisIBSSIBO
SymptomsAbdominal pain (RIF), diarrhoea (non-bloody often), weight loss, fatigue, perianal disease (fistulae, abscess), mouth ulcersBloody diarrhoea, urgency, tenesmus, LIF painAbdominal pain relieved by defecation, bloating, altered habit; no weight loss or bleedingBloating, diarrhoea, steatorrhoea, B12 deficiency
SignsRIF mass, clubbing, perianal skin tagsUsually few; fever/tachycardia if severeNormal
Key IxCalprotectin ↑, ileocolonoscopy (skip lesions, cobblestoning), MR enterography, histology (granulomas)Calprotectin ↑, colonoscopy (continuous from rectum), histology (crypt abscesses)Rome IV; exclude coeliac, FBC, CRP, calprotectin, CA-125 (women)Glucose/lactulose hydrogen breath test
IBD differentials
  • Infective colitis (send stool cultures, C. difficile)
  • Coeliac
  • Microscopic colitis (older women; normal-looking colon, biopsy)
  • Colorectal cancer
  • Diverticulitis
  • Ischaemic colitis
  • NSAID enteropathy
  • IBS.
Investigations in IBD
  • FBC (anaemia, ↑ platelets)
  • CRP/ESR
  • Albumin
  • LFTs (PSC)
  • Ferritin
  • B12/folate
  • Faecal calprotectin (>250 suggests IBD)
  • Stool MC&S + C. difficile toxin
  • Colonoscopy + biopsy (gold standard)
  • Flexible sigmoidoscopy in acute severe UC (avoid full colonoscopy: perforation risk)
  • AXR (toxic megacolon >6 cm)
  • CT (abscess, perforation).
Acute severe UC (Truelove & Witts)
  • ≥6 bloody stools/day + systemic toxicity (fever, HR >90, Hb <105, ESR >30) → admit, IV hydrocortisone, VTE prophylaxis, stool cultures
  • Rescue therapy (ciclosporin/infliximab) or colectomy by day 3–5 if not responding.
Treatment principlesInduce remission → maintain remission; stop smoking (Crohn's); nutrition; MDT (IBD nurses, surgeons, dietitians); surveillance colonoscopy for cancer.

los.text: Describe micro-organisms normally present in the bowel and the common pathogens of the gastrointestinal tract
los.html:
Normal gut flora (microbiome)
  • Density increases distally: stomach (very few: acid; H. pylori, lactobacilli)
  • → small intestine (10³–10⁸/mL; streptococci, lactobacilli, enterobacteria in ileum)
  • → colon (~10¹¹–10¹²/g; >99% anaerobes: Bacteroides, Clostridium clusters, Bifidobacterium, Faecalibacterium; plus E. coli, enterococci).
Functions
  • Fermentation of fibre → short-chain fatty acids (butyrate = colonocyte fuel)
  • Vitamin K and B vitamin synthesis
  • Bile acid metabolism
  • Colonisation resistance against pathogens
  • Immune development (Tregs, IgA).
DysbiosisAntibiotics → C. difficile; ↓ diversity in IBD, obesity; SIBO (↓ motility, strictures, blind loops, PPIs).
Common GI pathogens
  • Bacteria: Campylobacter jejuni (commonest UK bacterial cause; undercooked poultry), Salmonella (non-typhoidal; eggs, poultry; S. Typhi/Paratyphi enteric fever), Shigella (dysentery, low infective dose), STEC/EHEC O157:H7 (bloody diarrhoea → HUS), ETEC (traveller's diarrhoea), Vibrio cholerae, C. difficile (toxins A/B; pseudomembranous colitis), Yersinia (mimics appendicitis), S. aureus and B. cereus (preformed toxins), Listeria, H. pylori.
  • Viruses: norovirus, rotavirus, adenovirus, sapovirus, astrovirus.
  • Protozoa: Giardia, Cryptosporidium, Entamoeba histolytica.
  • Helminths: threadworm, roundworm, tapeworm.
Infections can trigger post-infectious IBS and IBD flares; Campylobacter → Guillain–Barré; Shigella/Salmonella → reactive arthritis.

los.text: Explain the pathophysiology and complications of IBS, IBD and bacterial overgrowth (focus on IBD)
los.html:
IBD

  • Pathogenesis: genes + environment + dysbiosis + barrier dysfunction → inappropriate immune response to gut flora.
    • Genes: NOD2/CARD15 (Crohn's), HLA, IL-23R; FHx.
    • Environment: smoking ↑ Crohn's risk but protects in UC; antibiotics, diet, Western lifestyle.
    • Immune: Crohn's = Th1/Th17 (IL-12, IL-23, TNF-α); UC = atypical Th2 (IL-13).
Crohn'sUC
DistributionMouth to anus, skip lesions, terminal ileum commonestRectum extending proximally, continuous, colon only (backwash ileitis)
DepthTransmuralMucosal
MacroscopicCobblestoning, deep fissuring ulcers, strictures, fistulae, fat wrappingDiffuse erythema, friable mucosa, pseudopolyps, loss of haustra ("lead pipe")
MicroscopicNon-caseating granulomas, lymphoid aggregatesCrypt abscesses, crypt distortion, goblet cell depletion
ComplicationsStrictures/obstruction, fistulae, abscesses, perianal disease, malabsorption (B12, bile acids), gallstones, renal oxalate stonesToxic megacolon, haemorrhage, colorectal cancer (risk ↑ with extent/duration), primary sclerosing cholangitis
  • Extraintestinal: enteropathic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, erythema nodosum, pyoderma gangrenosum, episcleritis/uveitis, PSC, VTE, osteoporosis, anaemia.

IBS

  • Disorder of gut–brain interaction: visceral hypersensitivity, altered motility, gut microbiota changes, low-grade inflammation, post-infectious, psychological stress/anxiety, central pain processing.
    • Subtypes: IBS-C, IBS-D, IBS-M.
    • Complications: impaired quality of life
    • no structural damage.

SIBO

  • ↑ bacteria in small bowel (stasis: strictures, blind loop, diverticula, diabetes/scleroderma dysmotility, PPIs)
    • → bile salt deconjugation (fat malabsorption, steatorrhoea), B12 consumption (deficiency; folate may be ↑), mucosal injury, gas
    • → bloating, diarrhoea, weight loss.
    • Rx: rifaximin/antibiotics, treat cause.

los.text: Apply the pharmacology of drugs used to treat IBS and IBD and relevant evidence for their benefits to be able to choose and manage effective treatment for individual patients
los.html:
DrugMechanismUseKey side effects
5-ASA (mesalazine)Topical anti-inflammatory (↓ prostaglandins, leukotrienes, NF-κB)UC: induction and maintenance (oral + rectal); little role in Crohn'sNephritis (monitor U&E), blood dyscrasias, pancreatitis
Corticosteroids (prednisolone, budesonide, IV hydrocortisone)Broad immunosuppressionInduce remission (not maintenance)Cushingoid, osteoporosis, diabetes, infection, mood
Thiopurines (azathioprine, mercaptopurine)Purine antimetabolites → ↓ lymphocyte proliferationMaintenance, steroid-sparingCheck TPMT before; myelosuppression, hepatitis, pancreatitis, lymphoma/skin cancer; allopurinol interaction
MethotrexateFolate antagonistCrohn's maintenanceTeratogenic, hepatotoxic, myelosuppression
Anti-TNF (infliximab, adalimumab)Neutralise TNF-αModerate–severe, fistulating Crohn's, ASUC rescueScreen TB/hepatitis B, infections, demyelination, lymphoma
VedolizumabAnti-α4β7 integrin (gut-selective)UC/Crohn'sFewer systemic infections
Ustekinumab / risankizumabIL-12/23 or IL-23 blockadeCrohn's, UC
JAK inhibitors (tofacitinib, upadacitinib), S1P modulators (ozanimod)Oral small moleculesUC (± Crohn's)VTE, infection (shingles)
CiclosporinCalcineurin inhibitorASUC rescueNephrotoxic, hypertension, seizures (low Mg²⁺/cholesterol)
SurgeryUC → colectomy (curative; ileoanal pouch); Crohn's → resections, stricturoplasty, fistula surgery (not curative).
IBS (NICE)
  • Diet (regular meals, fibre adjustment, low-FODMAP under dietitian)
  • Antispasmodics (mebeverine, hyoscine, peppermint oil)
  • Laxatives for IBS-C (not lactulose; linaclotide if refractory)
  • Loperamide for IBS-D
  • Low-dose tricyclic antidepressant (amitriptyline 5–10 mg, neuromodulator) second line
  • Then SSRI
  • CBT/hypnotherapy.
SIBORifaximin or other antibiotics; treat underlying cause.

los.text: Describe the key signs and symptoms, and functional and morphological changes in common large and small intestine disease states
sessions: Path: Small and large bowel pathology
los.html:
DiseaseSigns & symptomsFunctional/morphological changes
Coeliac diseaseDiarrhoea, bloating, weight loss, iron/folate deficiency, dermatitis herpetiformisVillous atrophy, crypt hyperplasia, ↑ intraepithelial lymphocytes (Marsh); proximal small bowel; ↓ absorptive surface
Crohn's diseaseSee LO 3Transmural inflammation, granulomas, fissures, strictures
Ulcerative colitisBloody diarrhoeaContinuous mucosal inflammation, crypt abscesses
Ischaemic bowel
  • Acute mesenteric ischaemia: severe pain out of proportion to signs, AF
  • Ischaemic colitis: LIF pain + bloody diarrhoea (splenic flexure watershed)
Mucosal necrosis → transmural infarction, gangrene
Infective colitisDiarrhoea ± blood, feverAcute self-limited colitis; pseudomembranes (C. difficile)
Diverticular diseaseLIF pain, altered habit; diverticulitis: fever, tenderness; bleedingMucosal herniation through weak points where vessels penetrate muscle (sigmoid); muscle thickening
Colorectal adenoma → carcinomaChange in bowel habit, rectal bleeding, iron-deficiency anaemia, mass, obstructionTubular/villous adenomas (dysplasia) → adenocarcinoma; APC → KRAS → TP53 pathway; MSI pathway (Lynch)
Small bowel obstructionColicky pain, vomiting, distension, absolute constipationDilated loops proximal; adhesions, hernias
Neuroendocrine tumoursCarcinoid syndrome (liver mets: flushing, diarrhoea, wheeze)Small bowel/appendix; chromogranin
Microscopic colitisChronic watery diarrhoea, older womenNormal mucosa; thickened subepithelial collagen band or ↑ lymphocytes
Hirschsprung's, Meckel's, appendicitisAganglionosis; ectopic gastric mucosa; luminal obstruction → inflammation
  • Common principles: loss of absorptive surface → malabsorption/diarrhoea; inflammation → bleeding, protein loss; obstruction → pain/vomiting; chronic inflammation → dysplasia/cancer.
